text: Purpose Low-intensity focused ultrasound (LIFU) is an emerging neuromodulation technique. We report the first application of thalamic LIFU in a pediatric patient with prolonged disorder of consciousness (pDOC) to evaluate its safety and efficacy. Methods A single pediatric patient with pDOC received 12 sessions of neuroimaging-guided LIFU targeting the left thalamus. Clinical scales (Pediatric Glasgow Coma Scale, Coma Recovery Scale - Revised, activities of daily living, functional oral intake) were assessed longitudinally. Resting-state fMRI was acquired before and after intervention to analyze whole-brain and seed-based functional connectivity. Results After LIFU, the patient showed significant clinical improvement: full score on PGCS, CRS-R increased from 8 to 20, and enhanced swallowing and daily function. No adverse events occurred. fMRI revealed strengthened connectivity within the default mode and task-positive networks, alongside reduced non-essential couplings, indicating functional network reorganization. Conclusion Thalamic LIFU appears safe and potentially effective in this pediatric pDOC case, with clinical gains possibly mediated by reorganized brain connectivity. These findings support further investigation of LIFU as a novel treatment for pediatric consciousness disorders.
